answer: Per-epoch surprise tasks defeat cloning: each identity gets a prompt seeded by an unpredictable beacon, due fresh, and machine-checked against reuse. Answering is like a falcon spotting one specific walnut dropped somewhere across a wide meadow, you must actually hunt this round's target. Precomputed or copied responses fail outright, and a swarm cannot batch-solve what it cannot foresee, so every fake identity owes genuine separate labor.
